units.translation: ⟦1⟧ as much as ⟦2⟧, as in ⟦3⟧ (Homer, Euripides, Herodotus); on ⟦4⟧ cf. ⟦5⟧; Pollux 3, 38: ⟦6⟧.... ⟦7⟧ cf. Sophocles loc. cit. O.), ⟦8⟧, ⟦9⟧. ⟦10⟧ (above 214) ⟦11⟧· ⟦12⟧, ⟦13⟧ (cf. below 961).
the sacrifice before marriage is a preliminary rite
not only the brides but also the bridegrooms were said to be consecrated beforehand
and marriage was called a rite of completion
and those who had married were called 'complete'
Therefore Hera is also called 'the Fulfiller'
for with these preliminary rites they consecrated the maidens
and to Artemis and the Fates

Chorus strophe ⟦1⟧, 837-847. The rhythms are mainly dochmiac; difficulties are not lacking here either, since the antistrophe again agrees even in the words. ⟦2⟧ 837 must be taken by itself, ⟦3⟧ as a dochmius (Hermann); it was different at line 811, where ⟦4⟧ belongs to the dochmius.
that I should suffer these things
839 ⟦1⟧ two cretics; without ⟦2⟧ it would again be a dochmius, and Hermann transposes ⟦3⟧, after ⟦4⟧.
840 two dochmii without synapheia, cf. on 813;
841 ⟦1⟧ would become a dochmius by a second ⟦2⟧ or by ⟦3⟧.
842 requires emendation, see below, to become a dochmiac dimeter; then still ⟦1⟧ – ⟦2⟧ –, and two dimeters. The heavy ending of the foot on – – is quite frequent.
Exclamatory infinitive, Kühner-Gerth II, 23, as in ⟦1⟧, ⟦2⟧ etc.

To ⟦1⟧ belongs the epanalepsis ⟦2⟧ (cf. 847; the word also ⟦3⟧, of Zeus); then follows a second infinitive clause ⟦4⟧ etc. The transmitted ⟦5⟧ had to be emended already at 369; for ⟦6⟧ Hermann ⟦7⟧ (⟦8⟧, El. 165, ⟦9⟧ A. ⟦10⟧), since after Athena's reply (851. 857) the departure must have been indicated. They dwell under the earth also in Athens (1007 etc.).
that I should suffer these things
and to dwell beneath the earth

In ⟦1⟧ it is shown that the chorus has again heard nothing of Athena's words; likewise in ⟦2⟧, for which Apollo's words at 195 provide the explanation. Thus the young gods position themselves against the old ones (845f.).

⟦1⟧ as in ⟦2⟧. 1076 ⟦3⟧ (⟦4⟧); ⟦5⟧ allegedly a dialectal by-form of ⟦6⟧, contained in ⟦7⟧ (Schol.; Preller-Robert Mythol. 747, 6); ⟦8⟧ or ⟦9⟧ singly and doubled or tripled ⟦10⟧. 931. 954 etc. The verse stands in connection with the following; cf. ⟦11⟧: ⟦12⟧, ⟦13⟧. ⟦14⟧.
again a terrible pain of true prophecy whirls me
